title: LETTER 4: Letter to RBI Governor — Suggestion on Digital Lending

blocks.content: Topic: Write a letter to the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India suggesting measures to regulate unregistered digital lending apps that are exploiting borrowers.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Letters addressed to regulatory heads require an official, analytical, and constructive tone with clearly delineated recommendations.
Digital lending suggestions focus on curbing illegal loan apps, enforcing data minimization, and ensuring transparent interest rate disclosures.
Key regulatory tools discussed include mandatory Key Fact Statements (KFS) and direct disbursement without third-party pool accounts.
Formal letter structure demands standard salutations, a precise subject line, structured arguments, and proper complimentary closing.

blocks.content: A robust regulatory framework for digital lending is essential to protect vulnerable borrowers while fostering responsible fintech innovation.
Subject: Suggestions for Strengthening Regulation of Digital Lending Applications

rows: Direct RE to Borrowers (per RBI Guidelines)

blocks.content: I write this letter as a concerned citizen and banking professional to seek your kind attention towards the growing menace of unregulated digital lending applications causing severe harm to vulnerable borrowers across India. Recent media reports and RBI's own advisories have highlighted incidents of harassment, data theft, and usurious interest rates being charged by entities operating outside the regulatory framework.

In 2021 and 2022, RBI's own Working Group on Digital Lending identified that out of hundreds of lending apps available on popular platforms, many were operated by unregistered entities using nominee names and foreign servers. Despite RBI's September 2022 Digital Lending Guidelines — which mandated that loan disbursements be made only to borrowers' bank accounts and prohibited third-party involvement in fund flows — enforcement remains challenging, particularly against fly-by-night operators who change their app names and structures frequently.

I respectfully suggest the following measures: (i) making it mandatory for all app stores to verify RBI registration before hosting any lending app; (ii) establishing a 'Digital Lending Registry' — a public database of all authorised digital lenders similar to SEBI's SCORES platform; (iii) making the Key Fact Statement (KFS) available in all 22 scheduled Indian languages; (iv) creating a dedicated 24x7 helpline for digital lending grievances, ring-fenced from the general Ombudsman portal; and (v) imposing civil and criminal penalties on payment aggregators who knowingly facilitate unregistered lenders.
I am confident that RBI's proactive stance will protect crores of Indian borrowers and uphold the integrity of India's financial system.

items: Ensure the subject line explicitly mentions the core proposal or suggestion for immediate clarity.
Use standard placeholders (e.g., XYZ, City ABC) for personal identity to adhere to competitive exam evaluation norms.
Highlight specific regulatory mechanisms like Regulated Entities (REs), Lending Service Providers (LSPs), and Grievance Redressal Officers.

blocks.content: Examiner's Tip: Letters to high officials (RBI Governor, Finance Minister) should be respectful and policy-oriented. Reference specific regulatory developments (Digital Lending Guidelines 2022) to show expertise. Suggest specific, actionable measures.
